function.description: Send a GET request to a specified URL to retrieve all products and branches with triangulation runs in the latest 90 days. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to send the GET request to.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The MIME types that are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request as a dictionary of header names to header values.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

days.description: The number of days to look back for triangulation runs.

end_date.description: The end date for the data retrieval period, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. If null, defaults to the current date.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the request.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to a certificate file to verify the peer.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names to cookie values.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary mapping protocol names to URLs of the proxies.

stream.description: If true, the response should be streamed; otherwise, the response will be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not.

message.content:
**What “EDAG” usually means**

In most contexts—especially when people talk about cars, design houses, or engineering services—the abbreviation **“EDAG” refers to the German‑based automotive engineering company *EDAG Automotive GmbH***.  
It’s one of Europe’s largest independent product development firms, offering everything from concept design and vehicle architecture to production support and digitalization solutions.

---

### A bit more on the name itself  

While the company has been around since the early 1970s, there isn’t a single, universally accepted expansion of the letters *EDAG*. Historically:

| Year | Context | What the letters stood for |
|------|---------|----------------------------|
| Early 70s | Founders’ initials + “Auto” | Often cited informally as **„E.D.A.G.“ – Einfaches Deutsches Auto­Gehäuse**, i.e., “Simple German Car Body”. |
| Today   | Brand identity | The letters are treated primarily as a trademark rather than an acronym. |

So if you see “EDAG” in a technical paper, press release, or job posting, it almost always points to this well‑known automotive engineering house.

---

### Other common meanings (outside automotive)

If you’re looking at different industries, “EDAG” might appear elsewhere, such as:

| Field | Possible Expansion | Notes |
|-------|--------------------|-------|
| IT / Networking | **E**xtensible **D**ata **A**ccess **G**ateway | Used in some enterprise software suites. |
| Healthcare | **E**mergency **D**ental **A**ssistance **G**roup | Local dental emergency service provider. |
| Finance | **E**xecutive **D**evelopment **A**nd **G**rowth | Consulting firm specializing in executive training. |

These alternate definitions tend to show up only within their specific niche communities.

---

#### Bottom line

When someone says “I’m working at EDAG”, they almost certainly mean the German automotive engineering company. Unless the conversation explicitly mentions another sector, you don’t need to worry about alternative interpretations.
